topicName: Cloud Load Balancing: HTTP(S), TCP, Internal Load Balancing
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Cloud Load Balancing in Google Cloud (GCP)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Google Cloud Load Balancing distributes user traffic across multiple instances of your application, reducing the risk of overload and improving performance. GCP offers various load balancing options, including HTTP(S), TCP, and Internal Load Balancing, each designed for specific use cases."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"HTTP(S) Load Balancing"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"HTTP(S) Load Balancing distributes HTTP and HTTPS traffic to backend instances. It operates at the application layer (Layer 7) and provides features like SSL termination, content-based routing, and integration with Google Cloud Armor for security."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Global Load Balancing: Distributes traffic across multiple regions, providing high availability and low latency for users worldwide."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"SSL Termination: Offloads SSL encryption and decryption from backend instances, reducing their CPU load."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Content-Based Routing: Routes traffic based on the URL, headers, or other request attributes."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Integration with Google Cloud Armor: Protects your applications from DDoS attacks and other web exploits."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"# Example gcloud command to create an HTTP(S) load balancer
gcloud compute forwarding-rules create http-forwarding-rule \
    --global \
    --target-http-proxy http-proxy \
    --ports 80"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"TCP Load Balancing"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"TCP Load Balancing distributes TCP traffic to backend instances. It operates at the transport layer (Layer 4) and is suitable for non-HTTP(S) traffic, such as databases, gaming servers, and other custom protocols."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Global Load Balancing: Distributes traffic across multiple regions for high availability."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regional Load Balancing: Distributes traffic within a single region."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Supports various TCP-based protocols."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"# Example gcloud command to create a TCP load balancer
gcloud compute forwarding-rules create tcp-forwarding-rule \
    --region us-central1 \
    --target-pool tcp-target-pool \
    --ports 8080"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Internal Load Balancing"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Internal Load Balancing distributes traffic to backend instances within your Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network. It allows you to create private services that are only accessible to other instances within your VPC."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regional Load Balancing: Distributes traffic within a single region."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Private Service Access: Enables secure communication between services within your VPC."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Supports both TCP and HTTP(S) traffic."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"# Example gcloud command to create an internal load balancer
gcloud compute forwarding-rules create internal-forwarding-rule \
    --region us-central1 \
    --subnet default \
    --target-pool internal-target-pool \
    --ports 80"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Choosing the right load balancer depends on your application's requirements. HTTP(S) Load Balancing is ideal for web applications, TCP Load Balancing for non-HTTP(S) traffic, and Internal Load Balancing for private services within your VPC. Consider factors like traffic type, global vs. regional scope, and security requirements when making your decision."}]
